classification.difficultyReason: Interpret a delayed start, calculate both speeds and model the meeting point.

content.prompt:
Two cyclists are riding on the same road between two points, A and B, which are 60 km apart. Cyclist $X$ starts first and is riding from B to A. Cyclist $Y$ starts 20 minutes later and is riding from A to B. The distance–time graph shows all the information.

Find:

spec.description: Arrowed axes without ticks or grid. Descending X segment and ascending Y segment cross without an intersection label. Coordinate labels and the red Y endpoint are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is permanently visible; no solution annotations are included.

children.prompt: how long it takes each cyclist to ride between A and B

answer.worked:
Read the start and finish times from the graph.

$$\begin{align*}T_X&=\frac{5}{2}-0\\T_X&=2\frac{1}{2}\text{ hours}\\T_Y&=2-\frac{1}{3}\\T_Y&=1\frac{2}{3}\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: how far from A they pass each other

inlines.text: Equate the cyclists’ distances from A, allowing for Y’s delayed start.

answer.worked:
Let $t$ hours be the time since $X$ started. Then $Y$ has travelled for $t-\frac{1}{3}$ hours. At their meeting point, their distances from A are equal.

$$\begin{align*}60-24t&=36\left(t-\frac{1}{3}\right)\\60-24t&=36t-12\\72&=60t\\t&=\frac{6}{5}\end{align*}$$

The distance from A is

$$\begin{align*}d&=60-24\times\frac{6}{5}\\d&=\frac{156}{5}\\d&=31.2\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$

Check: $36\left(\frac{6}{5}-\frac{1}{3}\right)=31.2$ km also.
